overview: The file consists of a single Department of State “List of Papers” sheet concerning copper in Japan. It records and summarizes a telegram sent by Neville from Japan on April 6, 1932, reporting that prevailing Japanese copper prices were unsatisfactory while the industry as a whole was nevertheless considered financially sound. The entry directs researchers to decimal-file reference 894.50/61 for the underlying telegram or related material.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. diplomatic official in Japan; sender of the referenced telegram

subfiles.title: List of Papers entry for Neville telegram on the Japanese copper industry
subfiles.from: Department of State; entry concerning a telegram from Neville in Japan
subfiles.about: The sheet summarizes and cross-references Neville’s April 6, 1932 telegram about copper prices and the financial condition of Japan’s copper industry.
subfiles.summary: This filing sheet records telegram no. 107, sent at 4 p.m. from Japan by Neville and identified as section F. According to its précis, copper prices in Japan were unsatisfactory, but the copper industry as a whole was said to remain in good financial condition. Researchers are directed to file 894.50/61 for the referenced material.

interest: The page is useful both as a concise snapshot of the Japanese copper industry in April 1932 and as evidence of State Department filing and cross-referencing practices. Its distinction between weak commodity prices and the industry’s generally sound financial position may help historians investigate how Japanese mining firms weathered the early-1930s economic downturn. The reference to 894.50/61 provides a lead to the fuller diplomatic report, which is not present here.
